beforeSession: Print the paper story seed packets, seed slips, and adult guide before the session; these are writing starters, not real seeds.
Set the adult-led rule: look, listen, point, sketch, and imagine from the yard, garden view, porch view, window view, table, or park edge.
Say that writers do not collect or touch outdoor materials; ideas come from safe looking and listening.
Choose one calm viewing option and one table writing option before writers arrive.
Keep the session screen-free, printable, offline, and short enough for one packet to become one story seed.
packetTableSetup: Place blank paper packets, pencils, and seed slips on the table where the adult can see every page.
Set six labeled piles: setting, character, object, sequence, revision, and sensory.
Put one broad place card on the table: yard, garden view, porch view, window view, table, or park edge.
Leave space for sketches so writers can point or draw before adding words.
Keep unused packets in an adult folder so the table stays calm and screen-free.
observationToStorySeeds: Ask each writer for one look detail, one listen detail, and one imagine detail.
Turn a color from the garden view into a setting seed with a mood word.
Turn a shape from the yard or porch view into an object seed with a job.
Turn a gentle sound from the window view or park edge into a sensory seed with a clue.
Finish each packet by choosing one sentence to save for a later printable story.
privacyAndSiteNotes: Use only broad place words: yard, garden view, porch view, window view, table, or park edge.
Use invented character labels or role words for every person in a story.
Leave private signs, numbers, family routines, and identifying details off the packet.
Keep finished packets with the family adult, tutor, homeschool co-op adult, or library table host.
Treat the packet as paper writing work, not material for a shared site.
familyHandoff: Give one finished paper packet and one blank seed slip to each writer.
Tell family adults that five to nine minutes is enough for one extra story seed.
Invite families to look, listen, point, sketch, and imagine from a yard, garden view, porch view, window view, table, or park edge.
Ask adults to praise one clear word, sketch, or sentence before offering one small revision idea.
Suggest keeping all packet pages together so a later writing session can reuse the strongest seed.
reset: Collect unused paper packets, seed slips, pencils, and broad place cards.
Check finished pages for private details before they leave the table.
Recycle scrap pages that only contain warm-up marks.
Restock the adult folder with fresh packets for the next offline session.

packetFormats.name: Window View Setting Packet
packetFormats.bestFor: A quiet family or tutoring start when the writer can observe without leaving the table.
steps: Adult places the packet beside a clear window view and reads the paper-only reminder.
Writer looks, listens, and points to one color, shape, or quiet sound.
Writer sketches the detail inside the packet flap.
Writer turns the detail into one setting seed sentence.

packetFormats.name: Garden View Character Packet
packetFormats.bestFor: Writers who need a friendly character idea from safe observation.
steps: Adult chooses one garden view and reminds the writer to observe without collecting or touching anything.
Writer points to one detail that seems calm, busy, tiny, bright, or hidden.
Writer imagines a made-up character who would notice that detail first.
Writer writes what the character wants, wonders, or carries in the story.

packetFormats.name: Yard Object Packet
packetFormats.bestFor: Parents and homeschool co-ops that want ordinary object prompts without outdoor handling.
steps: Adult names the yard as the viewing choice and keeps the writing at the table.
Writer looks for one nonliving thing already visible from the chosen view.
Writer sketches it as a pretend object with a helpful job.
Writer writes one object seed with what it does in the story.

packetFormats.name: Porch View Sensory Packet
packetFormats.bestFor: Kids who notice sounds and textures through safe looking and listening.
steps: Adult sets the packet at the table with porch view as the observation choice.
Writer listens for one gentle sound and looks for one color or pattern.
Writer chooses the detail that feels most story-ready.
Writer writes one sensory seed that tells what the detail might mean.

packetFormats.name: Table Revision Packet
packetFormats.bestFor: Library tables or tutors helping writers strengthen a seed they already started.
steps: Adult places an earlier paper packet and a blank revision slip on the table.
Writer reads or hears one sentence from the packet.
Writer adds one clearer look, listen, sketch, or imagine detail.
Writer copies the stronger sentence into the revision seed space.

packetFormats.name: Park Edge Sequence Packet
packetFormats.bestFor: Adult-led groups that can sit or stand at a park edge and write one short beginning path.
steps: Adult chooses the park edge view and keeps the group beside the adult.
Writer looks left, center, and right while staying with the adult.
Writer picks three safe-to-see details and orders them as first, next, and later.
Writer writes one sequence seed that uses those three details.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Yard Setting Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Look from the yard or window view. Write one color or shape you notice: ____________________. Make it a made-up setting detail: ____________________.
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: Our setting seed makes the place feel ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Garden View Character Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Look at the garden view without collecting anything. Imagine who would notice one detail first: ____________________. That character wants ____________________.
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: The character would begin by asking ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Table Object Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Choose one paper packet picture or table object. It looks like ____________________. In the story, its job is ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: First Next Later Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: The step we want to write more about is ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Add One Look Detail
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Reread a seed sentence. Add one look detail here: ____________________. New sentence: ____________________.
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: The revision made the sentence clearer by adding ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Sound From the Window View
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Listen from the window view. One gentle sound is ____________________. In the story, it means ____________________.
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: The sound clue tells the character ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Park Edge Place Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Look from the park edge and choose one safe-to-see detail: ____________________. Turn it into a setting seed: ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Helpful Object Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Point to one nonliving thing visible from the yard or table. It could become ____________________. Its story job is ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Quiet Character Choice
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Imagine a character who stays calm and notices carefully. The character notices ____________________ and decides ____________________.
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: The character choice we like is ____________________.

takeHomeSeedSlips.title: Better Ending Seed
takeHomeSeedSlips.direction: Choose one ending idea. Add a clearer setting, object, or sound detail: ____________________. Better ending: ____________________.
takeHomeSeedSlips.familyLine: The ending now feels more finished because ____________________.

optionalSharePrompts: Show one packet title or sketch if you choose: ____________________.
Read one setting seed from the paper packet: ____________________.
Point to the detail that became a story clue: ____________________.
Tell which broad place word helped today: ____________________.
Share one made-up character choice without private details: ____________________.
Show one object seed and its story job: ____________________.
Name one sentence that improved after revision: ____________________.
Keep the packet private today and mark the seed you want to save: ____________________.
